text: Recommended build: 88 of 88 random drops ended on the base (3 runs × 6 bodies, each re-dropped 1 s after coming to rest), and 36 of 36 set-downs ended on the base: each of the 36 wrong faces once (6 per band, S1…S6). Time to rest: median 9.0–9.3 s per drop run.
Steel-dowel build: 78 of 78 drops and 36 of 36 set-downs ended on the base.

How it moves. From a high band it tips band by band to the base, then rocks back up through the low bands (in the simulation, at most up to S5 after a set-down on S6) with decreasing swings, and settles after 5–10 s. It does not stop on any band on the way. That is what a low centre of mass and nearly flat bottom bands give: a faceted Weeble. Real PLA damps the impacts more than the simulation's restitution, so expect a quicker settle.

Run at the real size (PP_SCALE = 1), 1/1200 s steps, in a copy of the gallery's Bille Drop harness (exhibits/Bille/reconstruction/w37/sim/w37-drop.lua, made via reconstruction/pla/sim/pla-drop.lua) with only the body list and its label changed. Contact, losses and detection are unchanged, and nothing was tuned.
